  "title": "LACVLA: Enforcing Language-Affordance Grounding via Consistency Objectives for Zero-Shot Cross-Category VLA Manipulation",
  "core_problem": "How can end-to-end VLA models achieve zero-shot affordance transfer to unseen object categories, given the empirical finding that current VLAs largely ignore language instructions (LIBERO-Plus, CVPR 2026; LangGap, Mar 2026) — a failure mode that is catastrophic for cross-category transfer where novel objects lack visual priors and language is the only available guide for spatial grounding?",
  "opportunity": "Recent diagnostic work has exposed a fundamental flaw in VLAs: LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2510.13626) shows VLAs are largely insensitive to language variations and tend to ignore language instructions entirely, exhibiting positional bias rather than genuine semantic understanding. LangGap (arXiv 2603.00592, Mar 2026) quantifies this: VLAs with 95%+ standard success largely ignore language; targeted data augmentation partially closes the gap (0%→90% single-task, 0%→28% multi-task) but proves fundamentally insufficient as semantic diversity increases. This language-ignoring failure is survivable in-distribution — visual priors and layout memorization compensate — but becomes catastrophic for cross-category zero-shot transfer, where the model encounters objects with no visual precedent and must rely on language to determine WHERE to interact. Spatial grounding approaches (ST4VLA, ICLR 2026; InternVLA-M1; SpatialVLA, RSS 2025) improve performance broadly but do not structurally guarantee language conditioning — a model can learn spatial shortcuts that generalize within training categories but fail on novel objects. LIBERO-Para (Mar 2026) quantifies this fragility: VLAs suffer 22–52pp success rate drops under paraphrased instructions, with 80–96% of failures from planning-level trajectory divergence. Shin (Mar 2026) attempts LLM-generated paraphrase augmentation but achieves only +1.71pp improvement, consistent with LangGap's finding that augmentation alone hits a ceiling. PPCL (EACL 2024) showed consistency regularization beats augmentation with 10× fewer samples in NLP. The opportunity: an affordance-gated architectural bottleneck with self-supervised consistency objectives that structurally force language to condition spatial grounding — making language a mandatory pathway for action generation rather than an ignorable input — enabling genuine cross-category zero-shot transfer without 3D sensors, expensive cross-category annotations, or modular decomposition.",
  "landscape": "The VLA-affordance landscape has five relevant lineages, none of which structurally enforces language conditioning of spatial affordance representations for cross-category transfer. (1) Spatially-guided VLAs: ST4VLA (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2602.10109) introduces dual-system spatial grounding (Qwen2.5-VL planner + DiT/DINOv2 action expert), achieving 95.9% LIBERO average (98.0% Spatial, 99.0% Object, 93.8% Goal, 92.6% Long), 72%/61% attribute/spatial paraphrase robustness (vs π₀: 32%/31%), and 62% on new object instances (vs π₀: 32%, GR00T N1: 46%). This is LACVLA's strongest baseline — the null hypothesis is 'does explicit affordance consistency add value beyond spatial grounding alone?' InternVLA-M1 (arXiv 2510.13778) extends this with affordance recognition and chain-of-thought reasoning in pre-training. SpatialVLA (RSS 2025, arXiv 2501.15830) introduces Ego3D Position Encoding and Adaptive Action Grids. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.12276) aligns VLM features with 3D foundation models without 3D input at inference. All improve spatial understanding but none guarantees language conditions the spatial representation — LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026) shows even top VLAs still ignore language. (2) Language grounding diagnostics: LIBERO-Plus (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2510.13626) reveals VLAs are insensitive to language and exhibit positional bias, with performance dropping from 95% to below 30% under camera/robot state perturbations. LangGap (arXiv 2603.00592, Mar 2026) confirms VLAs ignore language and shows data augmentation's ceiling (28% multi-task). LIBERO-Para (arXiv 2603.28301, Mar 2026) quantifies paraphrase fragility (22–52pp drops). Shin (arXiv 2603.16044, Mar 2026) achieves only +1.71pp via augmentation. Stable Language Guidance / RSS (ACL 2026, arXiv 2601.04052) addresses modality collapse at inference via residual steering — complementary to LACVLA's training-time approach. (3) Modular affordance-then-action pipelines: RT-Affordance (arXiv 2411.02704), UAD (ICRA 2025), RAM (CoRL 2024), RAAP (arXiv 2603.29419, Mar 2026), AffordDP (CVPR 2025), RoboMAP (arXiv 2510.10912), A0 (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2504.12636), and GLOVER++ (CoRL 2025, arXiv 2505.11865) all produce affordance representations but feed them to separate downstream planners/policies, sacrificing end-to-end optimization. A0 achieves zero-shot cross-category transfer via 1M contact points but without language conditioning of the affordance representation. (4) Affordance-aware VLA reasoning and pre-training: CoA-VLA (ICCV 2025) and Sim2Real VLA (ICLR 2026) incorporate affordances via text chains. PokéVLA (arXiv 2604.20834, Apr 2026) pre-trains a VLM on HOVA-500K for affordance understanding, validating ego-centric→VLA transfer, but uses affordance only for backbone pre-training rather than as an explicit consistency objective. (5) Architectural bottleneck enforcement: DIAL (arXiv 2603.29844, Mar 2026) enforces a latent intent bottleneck via inverse dynamics — the action head MUST use predicted latent intent because it resolves the discrepancy between current and predicted states. This inspires LACVLA's affordance-gated bottleneck (stop-gradient on VLM features before action head, affordance map as spatial attention gate). (6) Cross-category zero-shot benchmarks: AGNOSTOS/X-ICM (arXiv 2505.15660) provides 23 unseen manipulation tasks for cross-task evaluation; VLA² (arXiv 2510.14902) uses agentic retrieval for unseen concepts. Gap: No existing work combines (a) architectural enforcement that language must condition spatial features, (b) self-supervised consistency objectives on affordance maps (not raw actions), and (c) cross-category zero-shot transfer as the primary evaluation target.",
  "approach": "We propose LACVLA, an end-to-end VLA that structurally forces language to condition spatial affordance grounding through an affordance-gated bottleneck and self-supervised consistency objectives, enabling zero-shot cross-category manipulation.

Architecture — Affordance-Gated Bottleneck (inspired by DIAL's latent intent bottleneck): Built on a 4B–7B VLM backbone (Qwen2-VL-4B via StarVLA or PaliGemma2) with LoRA fine-tuning. The architecture has three components:
(a) Affordance Readout: A cross-attention layer where language instruction tokens attend over intermediate VLM visual features (layer ~16 of 32 for Qwen2-VL), producing a dense affordance heatmap over the image. This encodes WHERE to interact, conditioned on the instruction. Architecture: single cross-attention + LayerNorm + linear projection to H×W heatmap, <5M parameters.
(b) Stop-Gradient Bottleneck: VLM intermediate visual features are passed through a stop-gradient before reaching the action head. The action head receives: affordance_heatmap ⊙ sg(VLM_visual_features) + proprioceptive_state. The affordance map acts as a spatial attention gate — if the model produces a uniform (language-ignoring) affordance map, the action head receives unselective visual features with no spatial focus, degrading performance. If the map collapses to a degenerate peak, the action head loses context. This structurally forces task-relevant WHERE information through the language-conditioned affordance bottleneck, preventing the bypass problem identified by reviewers. Unlike a soft bottleneck, the stop-gradient ensures no task-semantic gradient flows through the non-affordance pathway — the action head CANNOT learn to extract task information from raw VLM features.
(c) Flow-Matching Action Head: A lightweight DiT (Diffusion Transformer) that generates trajectory chunks conditioned on the affordance-gated visual features + proprioceptive state, following the flow-matching formulation.

Training Objectives — Three jointly optimized losses with phased schedule:
(1) Instruction-Paraphrase Affordance Consistency (IPAC): Given the same visual scene and K LLM-generated paraphrases of the same task instruction (e.g., 'grab the mug handle' vs. 'grasp the cup by its handle'), the affordance maps must be consistent (KL divergence penalty on spatial heatmaps). This transfers the consistency regularization principle from PPCL (EACL 2024) — which showed consistency > augmentation with 10× less data in NLP — to spatial affordance heatmaps. Unlike Shin (2026), who uses paraphrases purely as data augmentation (achieving marginal +1.71pp), IPAC uses them as a regularization signal constraining affordance geometry. Paraphrases generated offline by LLM — free, unlimited supervision.
(2) Instruction-Discriminative Affordance (IDA): Given the same visual scene and two semantically different instructions (e.g., 'pick up the mug by its handle' vs. 'pour from the mug'), the affordance maps must diverge (margin-based divergence loss). This prevents degenerate consistency collapse where the model produces instruction-invariant heatmaps to trivially satisfy IPAC. Different-instruction pairs come naturally from multi-task robot datasets.
(3) Action-Grounded Affordance (AGA): Standard flow-matching loss for trajectory prediction through the affordance-gated bottleneck. This grounds the affordance map in manipulation-relevant contact regions via end-to-end backpropagation through the gating mechanism.

Phased Training Schedule:
Phase 1 — Affordance Readout Pre-training on HOVA-500K: Train the cross-attention readout to predict contact-point Gaussian heatmaps (σ proportional to object scale) conditioned on action-label text prompts from HOVA-500K's 675 action categories. Viewpoint augmentation (random crop, perspective warp, ego→third-person style augmentation) addresses the ego-centric domain gap. Diagnostic checkpoint: evaluate pre-trained affordance readout on robot observation images; if domain gap degrades affordance quality below threshold, bridge with (a) a small set of robot data with pseudo-affordance labels from action-contact heuristics and (b) cross-domain contrastive loss between HOVA-500K and robot VLM features for same-action categories. This addresses the reviewer concern that PokéVLA's backbone pre-training transfer is fundamentally different from affordance readout pre-training — we validate empirically before proceeding.
Phase 2 — End-to-end VLA training (steps 0–N): Fine-tune full model (VLM via LoRA + pre-trained affordance readout + flow-matching action head) on robot data. Sub-phases: (2a) AGA only for 10% of training — establish action grounding baseline. (2b) Add IPAC at 10% — enforce consistency while action loss stabilizes gradients. (2c) Ramp IDA from 0 to full weight over 15% of training via linear warmup, monitored by: (i) affordance entropy H(A) — if H(A) < 0.3 × H_max, increase IDA weight by 50%; (ii) instruction-discriminability D = mean pairwise KL between different-instruction maps on validation set — if D < 0.5, halt IPAC and boost IDA. GradNorm-style gradient normalization across the three losses balances training rates automatically.

Why Affordance Maps (Not Raw Actions) for Consistency: Affordance maps capture WHERE to interact — the geometric invariant across paraphrases and across categories sharing functional parts. Action distributions conflate WHERE + HOW + WHEN (trajectory shape, timing, force), making consistency regularization noisier. For cross-category transfer, WHERE is what transfers (handle locations generalize across mugs/cups/pitchers), while HOW adapts to object-specific geometry. This argument is validated empirically by ablation #6.

Cross-Object Functional Consistency via HOVA-500K: Group HOVA-500K images by shared action labels (675 categories) and apply soft KL penalty between affordance maps of same-action images from different object categories. This provides weak supervision for cross-category affordance consistency without requiring part-level functional equivalence annotations.

Data Pipeline: Open X-Embodiment and DROID for robot trajectories, HOVA-500K for affordance pre-training and cross-object grouping, LLM-generated instruction paraphrases (Qwen3 or GPT-4) for IPAC pairs.

Ablation Design (8 variants, addressing all reviewer concerns):
(1) Full LACVLA — affordance-gated bottleneck + IPAC + IDA + AGA
(2) No affordance bottleneck — direct VLA, no affordance readout (tests whether bottleneck is necessary)
(3) Modular composition — frozen GLOVER++ affordance → separate policy (tests end-to-end vs. modular)
(4) No consistency losses — only AGA through affordance bottleneck (tests whether architectural bottleneck alone suffices without consistency enforcement)
(5) Shin-style augmentation — paraphrases added as training data, no consistency loss (tests data augmentation ceiling, paralleling PPCL's NLP finding)
(6) IPAC on raw actions — KL divergence between action distributions under paraphrased instructions, no affordance readout (CRITICAL: tests whether isolating WHERE via affordance maps outperforms consistency on conflated action distributions — if affordance maps win, that's the paper's key finding; if raw actions work comparably, the affordance readout is unnecessary overhead)
(7) ST4VLA-style spatial grounding + IPAC on features — spatial grounding pre-training + consistency on intermediate VLM features without affordance readout (tests whether explicit affordance structure adds value beyond strong spatial pre-training + consistency, addressing the 'why not just do spatial grounding?' question)
(8) No phased training — all losses from step 0 (tests curriculum importance)

Evaluation Protocol — Primary (Cross-Category Zero-Shot Transfer):
(a) Held-out object category experiments: partition LIBERO/DROID object categories into train/test sets, test on entirely unseen categories with both standard and paraphrased instructions
(b) HOVA-500K cross-category transfer tests: train on K action categories with one set of objects (e.g., 'pour from pitcher'), test on same actions with different object categories (e.g., 'pour from kettle') — constructed from HOVA-500K's 675 shared action labels
(c) AGNOSTOS benchmark (arXiv 2505.15660) for cross-task zero-shot evaluation (23 unseen tasks)
(d) Real-world evaluation on 5+ unseen object categories across at least 3 manipulation primitives (grasp, pour, push)

Evaluation Protocol — Secondary:
(e) LIBERO-Para benchmark with PRIDE metric for paraphrase robustness (direct comparison with ST4VLA's 72%/61%)
(f) LangGap protocol for language grounding quality (targeting improvement over the 28% multi-task ceiling)
(g) Affogato for affordance quality assessment
(h) Standard LIBERO (Spatial, Object, Goal, Long) for in-distribution comparison with ST4VLA (95.9% avg)

# LangForce Paper Summary

## Full Title
"LangForce: Bayesian Decomposition of Vision Language Action Models via Latent Action Queries"

## Authors
Shijie Lian, Bin Yu, Xiaopeng Lin, Laurence T. Yang, Zhaolong Shen, Changti Wu, Yuzhuo Miao, Cong Huang, Kai Chen

## Abstract
The paper addresses a critical problem in Vision-Language-Action models where "language instructions are highly predictable from visual observations alone" leading to what researchers call "Information Collapse." This causes models to ignore language input and fail in out-of-distribution scenarios.

## Core Approach
LangForce uses a dual-branch architecture with learnable Latent Action Queries to:
- Estimate a vision-only prior p(a|v)
- Estimate a language-conditioned posterior π(a|v,ℓ)
- Optimize policy by maximizing conditional Pointwise Mutual Information between actions and instructions

This mechanism penalizes vision shortcuts and rewards actions that explicitly respond to language commands.

## Key Results
- **11.3% improvement** on the challenging out-of-distribution SimplerEnv benchmark
- Demonstrated across SimplerEnv and RoboCasa evaluation environments
- Achieves robust language grounding in robotic manipulation without requiring new training data

## Classification
Artificial Intelligence, Computation and Language, Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition, Robotics

# ProGAL-VLA: Overview and Key Details

## Full Title and Authors
**Title:** ProGAL-VLA: Grounded Alignment through Prospective Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models

**Authors:** Nastaran Darabi and Amit Ranjan Trivedi

## What is ProGAL-VLA?

ProGAL-VLA addresses a critical limitation in robotic vision-language-action models: their tendency to ignore language instructions and rely on visual cues instead. The system comprises three core components: an entity-centric 3D graph structure (GSM), a symbolic sub-goal planner, and a grounding mechanism that links abstract goals to concrete visual entities.

## Language Conditioning Mechanism

The model enforces language sensitivity through a **Grounding Alignment Contrastive (GAC) loss**, which implements entity-level constraints inspired by InfoNCE bounds. Critically, all actions condition on a "verified goal embedding" whose attention entropy serves as an internal ambiguity detector, enabling the system to recognize when instructions are unclear or contradictory.

## The Verification Bottleneck

The verification bottleneck functions as a deliberate constraint that increases "mutual information of language-actions." Rather than a limitation, this design choice ensures the model maintains tight coupling between linguistic instructions and corresponding actions, preventing the visual shortcuts that plague standard VLA models.

## Benchmark Results

**LIBERO-Plus:**
- Robustness under perturbations: 30.3% → 71.5%
- Language ignorance reduction: 3–4x improvement
- Entity retrieval: 0.41 → 0.71 Recall@1

**Custom Ambiguity Benchmark:**
- AUROC: 0.81 (vs. baseline 0.52)
- AUPR: 0.79
- Ambiguity clarification: 0.09 → 0.81 success rate

The paper addresses three key limitations in Vision-Language-Action models: architectural bias causes models to miss visual details, excessive visual tokens hinder attention focus, and task-irrelevant information creates noise. **FocusVLA's Two Main Innovations:**

1. **Modality Cascaded Attention**: This mechanism "eliminate[s] shortcut pathways, thereby compelling VLA models to rely on task-relevant visual details" for action generation. By removing these shortcuts, the model cannot bypass visual information processing.

2. **Focus Attention**: This technique "dynamically selects task-relevant visual patches to control information quantity while explicitly modulating their influence to suppress task-irrelevant noise."

## Results
Experiments on simulated and real-world robotic benchmarks demonstrate that FocusVLA "effectively leverages visual details to perform dexterous manipulations" and "substantially improves performance and accelerates convergence across a variety of tasks."

The research validates that VLA performance limitations stem primarily from visual information utilization rather than representation quality.

## Title
"CAST: Counterfactual Labels Improve Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models"

## Authors
Catherine Glossop, William Chen, Arjun Bhorkar, Dhruv Shah, Sergey Levine

## Abstract
The research addresses limitations in robot instruction-following by proposing a dataset augmentation technique. The core challenge is that "current vision-language-action (VLA) models struggle with following fine-grained commands" due to insufficient semantic diversity in existing datasets.

## What is CAST?
CAST is a method for enhancing VLA models by generating alternative language descriptions and corresponding actions for existing robot trajectories. Rather than collecting new data, it leverages vision-language models to create counterfactual labels that increase linguistic grounding diversity.

## How Counterfactual Augmentation Works
The technique automatically generates varied language annotations paired with different action trajectories for the same observations. This synthetic diversification enriches the training dataset without requiring additional real-world robot interactions, improving the model's ability to understand nuanced instructions.

## Results
Testing across indoor and outdoor navigation scenarios showed substantial improvements: the method achieved "27% increase in success rate on navigation tasks" while remaining competitive with established approaches, demonstrating effectiveness without extra data collection overhead.

# LangForce: Key Technical Details

## 1) Loss Function & Bayesian Objective

The core objective maximizes **Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI)** between actions and instructions:

**LLR Objective:**
```
ℒ_LLR = log p(ℓ|a,v) - log p(ℓ|v)
```

This formulation penalizes vision shortcuts by requiring actions to explain instruction semantics beyond what vision alone reveals.

**Total Training Loss:**
```
ℒ_total = (1-λ)ℒ_FM(ψ;H_Q^post) + λℒ_FM(ψ;H_Q^prior) - βℒ_LLR
```

Where λ=0.3, β=0.1. The dual branches use Flow Matching losses on posterior (vision+language) and prior (vision-only) branches, with "stop-gradient operations to prevent trivial optimization."

## 2) Backbone Model

**Qwen3-VL-4B** within the StarVLA framework (QwenGR00T architecture). The method introduces 64 learnable **Latent Action Queries** as tokens interfacing between VLM and Diffusion Transformer action head.

## 3) Benchmark Results

**LIBERO (Avg@500):** 98.4% (vs. baseline 96.5%)
- Spatial: 99.2% | Object: 99.6% | Goal: 99.4% | Long: 95.2%

**SimplerEnv (Avg@480):** 66.5% average success
- +11.3% improvement over baseline (55.2%)

**RoboCasa (Avg@50):** 52.6% average success across 24 tasks
- Surpasses baseline (47.8%), Isaac-GR00T N1.6 (47.6%)

## 4) Cross-Category Zero-Shot Transfer

**Real-world vegetable pick-and-place:** 80.8% success (97/120 trials) vs. baseline 59.2%. Tests generalization to unseen object categories—eggplant, pepper, carrot, cucumber—demonstrating "transfer beyond colored-block manipulation to real objects."

## 5) Training Compute

Training distributed across **8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs** for 50k steps (batch size 16 per device). No explicit FLOPs or wall-clock time provided.

## 6) Ablation Results

**+ Action Query only:** 57.5% on SimplerEnv (vs. baseline 55.2%)
**Full LangForce:** 63.5% → 66.5% (final reported)

The "+6.0% boost from full method validates that gains stem from the dual-branch PMI objective rather than architecture alone."

# ProGAL-VLA: Key Technical Details

## 1) GAC Loss Formulation
The Grounding Alignment Contrastive loss is: "ℒ_GAC = −log exp(sim(q,k⁺)/τ) / ∑_i exp(sim(q,k_i)/τ)" where q represents the symbolic sub-goal embedding and k values represent grounded entity embeddings, with temperature parameter τ.

## 2) Backbone Model
ProGAL-VLA uses OpenVLA-7B (based on LLaMA-2 architecture) as its action policy backbone. The prospective planner employs Qwen-2.5-VL-Instruct-7B, though this operates asynchronously once per episode only.

## 3) Benchmark Results
On LIBERO-Plus: robustness under robot perturbations improved from 30.3% to 71.5%; language ignorance reduced by 3-4x; entity retrieval improved from 0.41 to 0.71 Recall@1 (N=8). On the Custom Ambiguity Benchmark: AUROC reached 0.81 versus 0.52 baseline; AUPR 0.79; clarification on ambiguous inputs increased from 0.09 to 0.81.

## 4) Verification Bottleneck Mechanism
The system enforces that "at ⊥ (L,O_t,M_{t−1}) | (g_t,q_t)" - meaning actions become conditionally independent from language once the verified goal embedding g_t exists. Only this verified embedding reaches the action policy, blocking ungrounded language influence.

## 5) Depth Sensor Requirements
Yes, the approach requires depth: "Metric3D (v2, ViT-L backbone)" provides depth estimates that convert 2D detections into 3D entity representations with pose and geometric attributes.

## 6) Zero-Shot Cross-Category Transfer
The paper does not report zero-shot transfer evaluations on unseen object categories. Evaluation focuses on LIBERO-Plus robustness to perturbations and the controlled Custom Ambiguity Benchmark.

## 7) Entity-Centric Graph Structure
The Grounded State Module maintains "G_t = {e_1, e_2, ..., e_n}" where each entity node encodes visual features, geometric pose, and semantic descriptors. Memory M_t maintains temporal continuity with bounded capacity N_max=16 using FIFO updates.

Phase 2 — End-to-end VLA training: Fine-tune full model on robot data. GradNorm-style gradient normalization across losses.

LangForce's published results show 98.4% LIBERO avg and 80.8% real-world on 4 unseen vegetables — but their cross-category evaluation uses same-primitive pick-and-place of visually similar objects, not functionally distinct categories requiring different WHERE-to-interact.)

Evaluation Protocol — PRIMARY (Cross-Category Zero-Shot Transfer — the headline metric):
(a) Held-out object category experiments: partition LIBERO/DROID object categories into train/test sets, test on entirely unseen categories with standard and paraphrased instructions
(b) HOVA-500K cross-category transfer tests: train on K action categories with one set of objects (e.g., 'pour from pitcher'), test on same actions with different object categories (e.g., 'pour from kettle') — constructed from HOVA-500K's 675 shared action labels
(c) AGNOSTOS benchmark (arXiv 2505.15660) for cross-task zero-shot evaluation (23 unseen tasks)
(d) Real-world evaluation on 5+ unseen object categories across at least 3 manipulation primitives (grasp, pour, push) with functionally distinct geometry — NOT just visually similar objects like LangForce's vegetable pick-and-place

(f) LangGap protocol for language grounding quality (vs. 28% multi-task ceiling)
(g) Affogato for affordance quality assessment
(h) Standard LIBERO (Spatial, Object, Goal, Long) for in-distribution comparison with ST4VLA (95.9% avg) and LangForce (98.4% avg)
(i) LIBERO-Plus robustness under perturbations (vs. ProGAL-VLA 71.5%)

## Summary of changes (Major Revision)

**Why major, not minor or pivot:** The core architecture (affordance-gated bottleneck + IPAC + IDA + AGA) remains sound, but the stagnation was caused by a positioning problem, not a technical one. The "VLAs ignore language → we fix it" framing is now crowded with 7+ concurrent solutions. The revision completely repositions the narrative.

**Key changes:**

1. **Reframed core problem & opportunity:** The headline is now **cross-category zero-shot transfer** (training on mugs → testing on pitchers/teapots), not language bypass. Language grounding is repositioned as a necessary intermediate step. The key insight: affordance heatmaps capture WHERE-to-interact — the geometric invariant that transfers across categories — while LangForce's action-level PMI conflates WHERE+HOW+WHEN and ProGAL-VLA's entity-level grounding requires instance recognition that fails on novel categories.

2. **New landscape lineage (6):** Added all 7 competing language conditioning methods — LangForce (action-level PMI, 98.4% LIBERO, code available via starVLA), ProGAL-VLA (entity-level + depth sensors, 71.5% LIBERO-Plus), CAG (counterfactual dual-branch), FocusVLA (cascaded attention), IGAR (inference-time attention recalibration), CAST (counterfactual augmentation), RSS (residual steering). Each is differentiated by the abstraction level they operate at.

3. **Added ablation #9 (LangForce-style PMI):** Dual-branch Bayesian decomposition on the same Qwen2-VL-4B backbone, without affordance readout. This is the paper's most important comparison — if LACVLA beats LangForce on cross-category transfer but matches in-distribution, it validates the entire thesis. LangForce's code is publicly available via starVLA, reducing reimplementation risk.

4. **Narrowed gap claim:** From "no work structurally forces language conditioning" to "no work uses affordance-specific spatial representations as the bottleneck medium for language-conditioned cross-category manipulation transfer."

5. **AAAI 2027 deadline verified:** Abstract Jul 21, full paper Jul 28 (confirmed from official CFP page).

6. **Resource estimates adjusted:** +1 ablation (~20-25h A100) and LangForce reimplementation overhead across all tiers.
